title: dedicated-autoscaler: priority routing + burst controls + improved utilization reporting
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Improved autoscaler to support per-priority burst controls and expose richer utilization metrics; backfills migration script included.
description:
Context and motivation:

This PR enhances the Dedicated fleet autoscaler to support priority-aware burst controls and to surface improved utilization reporting for fleet ops and customers. Customers running mixed-priority workloads (gold/silver/free) were observing unfair burst consumption and poor visibility into how burst tokens and smoothing interact with throughput guarantees. This change provides: 1) per-priority tokenbucket/burst limits; 2) configurable smoothing parameters; 3) additional metrics and labels for utilization and burst consumption; and 4) migration/backfill to populate historical reporting.

What changed (high-level):
- Autoscaler: new priority routing path that accounts for per-priority burst budgets before scaling decisions.
- Tokenbucket: introduced per-priority bucket config and smoothing window to avoid capacity hogging.
- Reporting: emit redwood.dedicated.fleet.utilization and redwood.dedicated.fleet.burst_consumption metrics with priority tags.
- Backfill: migration script to compute priority-tagged utilization for past 30 days for UI/warn rules.

Commits (summary):
- Add per-priority tokenbucket state and enforcement (3fd2a1b)
- Wire priority labels through request routing and autoscaler logic (7b4f9c2)
- Export new Prometheus metrics and update Grafana dashboard templates (a8c7e23)
- Backfill script and migration for historical utilization (c0ffee1)

Changed files (high-level):
- services/autoscaler/src/autoscaler/priority_tokenbucket.py (new)
- services/autoscaler/src/autoscaler/priority_routing.py (mod)
- services/autoscaler/tests/test_priority_tokenbucket.py (new)
- observability/metrics/dedicated_metrics.go (mod)
- observability/grafana/dashboards/dedicated_utilization.json (mod)
- infra/migrations/20260218_priority_util_backfill.py (new)
- docs/dedicated/autoscaler.md (mod)
- examples/dedicated/priority-config.yaml (mod)

Small illustrative snippet (autoscaler config example):

priority_buckets:
  gold:
    burst_capacity: 2000  # max tokens
    refill_rate: 500      # tokens/sec
    smoothing_window_secs: 30
  silver:
    burst_capacity: 800
    refill_rate: 200
    smoothing_window_secs: 60

Review conversation (selected):
- Jin Li (reviewer): "Major +1 for the metrics and tests. One concern: the tokenbucket locking around state updates needs to avoid introducing contention in the hot path. Can we use sharded locks per-priority?"
- Author (Ethan Park): "Yes implemented sharded locks keyed by priority in 7b4f9c2; microbenchmarks show <1% added latency at 95th percentile for single-request path. Added tests for concurrent updates."
- Priya Khanna (reviewer): "Can the new metrics be consumed by existing alerting rules? We should avoid breaking existing dashboards."
- Author: "We added priority tags but kept the base metric names and a compatibility label (priority=all) for existing rules; updated Grafana templates include migration notes."
- Diego Ramos (reviewer): "Backfill looks expensive what's the rollout plan?"
- Author: "Backfill runs as a Kubernetes Job with rate limiting; we also added a dry-run mode. Will coordinate with SRE to run during off-peak and watch for API throttling."

CI and validation notes:
- Unit and integration tests added for tokenbucket, routing paths and metrics.
- Benchmarks: lightweight throughput tests show autoscaler decision latency unchanged within noise; tokenbucket enforcement reduces burst violation incidents in simulation by ~92%.

Rollout and migration plan:
1) Deploy autoscaler with feature flag (priority_buckets_enabled=false) to main for canary.
2) Enable feature flag for internal fleets and run backfill in dry-run to validate results.
3) Enable for production fleets in stages (per-region) with SRE monitoring.
4) After 2 weeks of stable telemetry, flip default feature flag to true and publish docs.

Notes on backwards compatibility:
- Existing configs without priority_buckets continue to behave as before: a single global tokenbucket is used.
- Metrics keep old names and include priority="all" to prevent alert churn.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Auto-recommend priority bucket values via Redwood Optimize workload analyzer.
- Per-customer soft quotas to avoid noisy neighbors across tenants.

This PR was reviewed, approved by reviewers, and merged by squashing commit series.
